summary.intent: Assess whether Phase 72 needed a discussion before planning, clean up drifted todos across Phases 70/70.1/71/72/73, then plan, execute, and ship Phase 72 (SDK write-plane durability/correctness) while triaging urgent desktop-e2e/web-e2e/sdk-e2e CI regressions that surfaced mid-session.
summary.outcome: Retired 8 stale Phase 71 todos and updated ROADMAP source lists; diagnosed and fixed three CI regressions across PR #601 (merged, FUSE seq-equivocation + D-16 driver fix + greptile perf opt) and PR #600 (merged, rotation-durability floor helper + sdk-e2e Test 21 idempotency + 4 web-e2e flake fixes, verified locally under CI-equivalent timeout regime then green in CI); Phase 72 was planned (10 plans/7 waves, plan-checker passed) and execution proceeded through Wave 3 (72-01 through 72-06 landed) before the transcript ends, with a new hardening plan (72-11) queued to fix vitest v3 Mock-type drift across test files and wire test-inclusive typechecking into CI.

repo: This repo closes todos by deleting them from pending/ and moving to completed/ via git mv, not by marking them done in place — an empty resolved/ folder does not mean nothing was completed, check completed/
Phase branches follow a `feat/<phase-slug>` naming convention that GSD auto-aligns to

ci-e2e.yml (Web E2E + Desktop E2E) triggers ONLY on push-to-main or workflow_dispatch, never on PRs — must dispatch manually with `gh workflow run <file> --ref <branch>` (the `-f ref=` form fails with 422 on workflows whose definition predates that input)

Playwright web-e2e ciFloor() helper only raises wait timeouts to 60s under CI (process.env.CI); local runs use the caller's raw (often 15-30s) timeout, causing IPNS-gated ops to reliably flake locally even when CI is fine — setting CI=1 locally also flips webServer.reuseExistingServer off, colliding with an already-running dev stack

pnpm typecheck in CI only runs each package's tsconfig.build.json (excludes tests) plus tsconfig.scripts.json — test files are never typechecked in CI even though the base tsconfig.json includes them, hiding a vitest v2→v3 Mock-generic migration drift across ~60+ test-file errors (sdk-core cas.test.ts/grant.test.ts, sdk ~12 files, api-client 1)
Local API server can silently run stale dist and reject TEST_LOGIN_SECRET after a source change — must restart from source
gsd executor sandbox cannot read .env, so any plan needing live secret-gated sdk-e2e runs must be deferred to phase-level verification where the orchestrator has .env access

code.finding: publish_file_node hardcoded seq=1 on first-publish gated only by 'inode cid empty', causing equivocation-gate 400s on stale UploadComplete replays; fixed by resolving IPNS first and routing Found outcomes into publish_with_cas_retry instead of skipping

publish_with_cas_retry gained an optional preresolved_seq param (greptile P2 perf fix) so the Found-path caller in content_ops.rs skips a redundant second IPNS resolve; conflict-retry path still always re-resolves since a pre-resolved value is stale after a conflict

Text editor / file content is re-resolved fresh from the live API on every open (downloadFromIpns→resolveIpnsRecord→resolveFileMetadata→downloadFileContent), never cached, which is why a naive single-read assertion after a restore races the in-flight republish

ciFloor() and waitForItemToDisappear/waitForItemToAppear apply a 60s floor to timeouts only under CI; local callers keep their explicit (often too-tight) timeout, the root cause of several full-workflow.spec.ts local flakes (4.10, 4.11)

workflow: When a background verification run cascades-fails at an unrelated early test, re-running with the same cold/warm stack repeatedly whack-a-moles between different ambient flakes — better to run once under the CI-equivalent timeout regime (temporarily patch config knobs like reuseExistingServer, then revert) rather than iterating many local reruns

When two PRs touch shared files serialized in dependency order, rebase the earlier-branched PR onto main after the dependency PR merges before dispatching validation CI, otherwise the dispatched run will fail on stale code from the unmerged dependency
Workflow-dispatched e2e runs are the correct way to get pre-merge runtime proof for workflows gated to push-to-main/dispatch-only triggers, avoiding a blind merge

Threading root-cause diagnosis through subagents (one per CI failure) and having each return an exact bug site + evidence let the orchestrator apply patches only after independently re-verifying signatures/schemas against production, rather than trusting agent output blindly

Capturing an unrelated but real, in-scope finding (vitest v3 Mock drift) as a durable todo file plus TaskCreate tracking entries preserved it across a long context-heavy session instead of losing it to compaction or scope creep

friction: GSD plan:pre hook JSON contains raw newlines/control characters inside string literals, breaking both `--raw` output parsing and a first lenient-parser attempt; required writing a dedicated escaping script before hook fragments (research, pattern-mapper, tdd, schema-gate) could be extracted

AskUserQuestion tool call for the discuss-vs-plan gate was answered with a meta-clarifying question from the user rather than a direct choice, requiring a follow-up read-through of all 9 todos to give a substantive answer

Multiple background local Playwright runs cascaded on different ambient flakes each time (4.10, then 4.11, then setup step 2.1, then 2.1 again), burning ~5 separate ~15-20min local runs before finally getting a clean signal by running under the CI timeout regime
Commit via lint-staged timed out at 2 minutes, apparently due to a hanging 1Password SSH signing prompt; had to verify out-of-band whether the commit actually landed
Earlier `git cat-file` checks used to verify whether todo completed/ moves were captured in HEAD gave inconsistent/wrong results, requiring a second decisive check to resolve
